annotations.title: Detect fillable fields in a flat PDF

description: Detect fillable form fields in a flat PDF (one with no form fields; pdf_inspect lists none): finds blanks drawn on the page as lines, boxes, underscores and checkboxes and returns a text or checkbox field for each, named from the nearest printed label, with a confidence from 0 to 1. Each entry has type, name, page, x, y, width, height in PDF points from the bottom-left of the page as the viewer sees it, the frame pdf_add_fields and pdf_edit use. The entries can be passed to pdf_add_fields as fields (label and confidence are ignored there), and pdf_fill then fills the result; pdf_add_fields with detect true does detection and adding in one call. Only drawn blanks are found: not a blank area with no line or box, a scanned image, or shaded cells with no outline. Results are suggestions: confidence scores are estimates, low-confidence entries can be wrong, and some detections are table cells or rules that are not blanks. Zero fields is a normal answer with a note. At most 200 fields per call; the pages argument describes continuing a large form. Read-only: the source is never modified.

max_pages.description: Analyse at most this many pages. Default 40. At most 100.

min_confidence.description: Drop fields below this confidence. Default 0.4 (drops only the weakest candidates, such as unlabelled shapes); 0.6 gives slightly higher precision and about a quarter fewer checkboxes.

pages.description: Pages to analyse, 1-based: "1-3,5,8-". Default: all pages (up to max_pages). Large forms: a call stops at its time and work limit, so while truncated is true the returned fields can be added with pdf_add_fields, after which pdf_detect_fields run on the resulting PDF with pages set to next_pages (exactly the pages not done, including a page cut at 200 fields; a sparse selection stays sparse) continues until truncated is false. Sending the original PDF again repeats the same names and is not supported. pages_skipped lists pages not analysed: reason too_complex (more drawn shapes or text than the per-page limits; sending them again gives the same answer) or deadline (the call stopped first; they are in next_pages).

password.description: Password to open the input, only needed for a user-password PDF (owner-locked files with an empty user password open without it).

pdf_path.description: PDF source: an https:// URL or a data:application/pdf;base64,… URI (this hosted server cannot read local file paths).

name: pdf_detect_fields

label.description: The printed label the name came from, empty if none

name.description: Taken from the nearest printed label; unique, no dot

x.description: Left edge in points from the page's left

y.description: Bottom edge in points from the page's bottom

next_page.description: First page not returned, or null when finished

next_pages.description: Page spec of exactly the pages not done (including a page cut at 200 fields), or null when finished

note.description: Present when no fields were found or pages were skipped

pages_skipped.description: Pages not analysed: too_complex (more drawn shapes or text than the per-page limits; sending them again gives the same answer) or deadline (the call stopped first; they are in next_pages)

truncated.description: The answer is incomplete (more pages than max_pages, more than 200 fields, or the call stopped at its limit): a further call on the PDF with the returned fields added and pages set to next_pages continues from there, and each call again covers at most max_pages pages. False means no page is left to continue; a page listed in pages_skipped as too_complex was not analysed and is never continued

title: Detect fillable fields in a flat PDF
